candidates.title: Their kids were exposed to carbon monoxide at a hockey rink. They're trying to prevent it from happening again
candidates.description: A group of Calgary parents is sharing their stories and concerns about the danger of carbon monoxide inside hockey arenas, after their own children were exposed to high levels of the odourless gas during a weekend tournament nearly two years ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario man found guilty of terrorism charge related to neo-Nazi group
candidates.description: An Ontario man was found guilty of participating in the activities of a terrorist group by an Ontario Superior Court judge Wednesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Free course covering basics of AI to be available to all Canadians by end of the year
candidates.description: With the artificial intelligence boom sweeping across Canada and around the world, the federal government is making efforts it says will ensure Canadians understand what AI is, what it can do and how it will impact them.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How are northern Sask. schools preparing youth for new mining opportunities?
candidates.description: Schools in northern Saskatchewan are adapting to prepare students to work in a mine that's under construction in the region. It's an unprecedented economic opportunity, but it doesn't come without concerns for the environment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa city council to consider motion to rename Trump Avenue
candidates.description: Ottawa city council is scheduled to vote on another proposal to rename a street named after U.S. President Donald Trump, who the local councillor says does not deserve the honour.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Average asking rents fall 4.8% in August as trade war adds fresh uncertainty: report
candidates.description: A monthly report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation says the August number marks the steepest year-over-year drop since March.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto blows past all-time record for lithium-ion battery fires
candidates.description: Lithium-ion batteries, particularly those used in e-bikes and e-scooters, have been linked to a growing number of fast-moving and unpredictable fires in Toronto.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: GlobalEye gamble: Ottawa chose surveillance plane without knowing it met military needs
candidates.description: Ottawa moved to acquire six GlobalEye surveillance aircraft without assurances they met military requirements — requirements not shared with competing manufacturers. Subsequent assessments identified capability gaps requiring modifications, raising questions about whether the Carney government’s push for speed, jobs and industrial benefits is taking precedence over the military’s operational needs.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stephenville, N.L., also saw stranded passengers on 9/11. Now, the community is telling the story on stage
candidates.description: The arts community in Stephenville is marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11 with a musical production about how that west coast town was affected by stranded passengers and turmoil at the local airport.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada was prepared to send ships to Iraq in 2003 if UN approved action, records show
candidates.description: Canada, a notable objector to the 2003 Iraq war, was preparing to back the U.S.-led invasion by sending naval ships into combat if the UN Security Council gave the go-ahead, according to cabinet records.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal police allegedly cut locs from people's hair. Here's the anti-Black history behind that
candidates.description: Sixteen police officers are under investigation over racist acts targeting Black and Arab people. Two historians explain how the alleged cutting and collecting of locs connects to a history of slavery, racism and control over Black bodies.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why N.S. rents are still increasing far faster than we saw historically for decades
candidates.description: For decades up to 2018, Nova Scotia's rent inflation rate was never higher than two per cent. Despite having slowed down in recent years, rent increases in the province are still at a rate at least several times higher than what we saw historically.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 85-year-old man killed by stray bullet inside Burnaby, B.C., home, investigators say
candidates.description: An 85-year-old man found dead in his Burnaby home is believed to be an innocent victim who was struck by a stray bullet, according to the Integrated Homicide Investigative Team (IHIT).
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada 'will NEVER be the 51st state. Sorry!': B.C. premier unveils new border welcome signs
candidates.description: B.C. Premier David Eby unveiled new welcome signs for U.S. border crossings at a Tuesday press conference, which he says reflect a message from his government: "Welcome to British Columbia, Canada. Strong, proud, and will NEVER be the 51st state. Sorry!"
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'It's been an absolute nightmare,' says man whose daughter was killed in Manitoba crash
candidates.description: Tom Borsa wants to see change at a Manitoba highway intersection where his 18-year-old daughter was among four people killed in a collision Sunday night.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Manitoba Labour Board orders striking Dynacare lab employees back to work
candidates.description: Hundreds of Dynacare workers are being ordered back to work by the Manitoba Labour Board, their union says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How are Trump’s Bombardier threats affecting Canada?
candidates.description: On Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump declared that Quebec-based aerospace company Bombardier would no longer be able to sell planes in the U.S. Shares in the company fell in early trading, but regained some of those losses later in the day Tuesday. Officials say it's not just Bombardier employees in Canada who could be affected.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Get ready to come home,' Wakeham says to former N.L. residents searching for Churchill Falls jobs
candidates.description: A rally-like celebration of the prospect of jobs tied to the Churchill Falls and Gull Island hydroelectric projects ended with a call from Newfoundland and Labrador Premier Tony Wakeham to trades workers who have previously left the province for work.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Separation making Alberta master of its destiny ‘a fiction,’ business leader says
candidates.description: With fewer than 45 days to go until the Alberta referendum, a provincial business organization has launched a new initiative intended to make the case for Alberta to remain in Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Renewed U.S.-Iran exchanges send oil price back over $100 US for first time in several weeks
candidates.description: Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, with the attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sending the international Brent crude benchmark over $100 US a barrel for the first time since July.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Apple unveils iPhone Duo, its new folding phone that costs at least $3K
candidates.description: Apple on Wednesday unveiled a foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company's flagship product.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: South Park pulls a Trump, to be renamed South America for new season
candidates.description: South Park appears to be taking a page out of Donald Trump's book: if you don’t like a name, change it. For its 29th season, the animated satire has announced a new title — and will be now known as South America.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China says it held 'candid and in-depth' military talks with Canadian officials last week
candidates.description: As the Carney government pursues deeper relations with Beijing, the Chinese government reports it held a "candid" exchange on military issues with Canadian officials earlier this month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bangladesh in grips of world's worst measles outbreak, with 1,000 dead in last 6 months
candidates.description: Bangladesh, which once came close to eliminating measles, is facing its worst outbreak on record, with around 1,000 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since March as hospitals struggle with overcrowding, shortages and a continuing influx of sick children.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drones a key part of Nepal's response to flash-flood disaster
candidates.description: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to ‌deliver relief to displaced people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Unhinged' for Canada to call dispute with U.S. a trade war, says Trump's tariff chief
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's top trade official says it's "unhinged" for Canadian leaders to characterize the administration's tariffs as a trade war against Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ben Shelton beats defending champ Carlos Alcaraz in U.S. Open match that ends after 3:30 a.m.
candidates.description: Ben Shelton had gone toe-to-toe with Carlos Alcaraz for five exhausting sets and finally, at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday, came the chance to end the U.S. Open champion's title reign.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: PWHL lands first season-long U.S. national broadcast deal with Scripps Sports for 4th season
candidates.description: The newly expanded PWHL enters its fourth season by securing its first season-long U.S. national broadcast deal with Scripps Sports, the women's hockey league announced on Wednesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump banning import of Canadian booze, motorcycles, other goods into U.S.
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is banning the import of Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and various other products into the U.S. as of Sept. 29. This latest move in an escalating trade war between Canada and the U.S. comes after Canadian retaliatory tariffs came into force on Tuesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Recent art thefts appear to be inspired by 2025 Louvre heist, art crime experts say
candidates.description: Art crime experts say last year's headline-grabbing Louvre heist seems to have inspired a rash of brazen art thefts, putting European museums holding valuable art in a tough spot. Thieves cut a hole in a fence and climbed through a window to steal four paintings from the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer on the French Riviera early Tuesday, local authorities said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vietnamese firm targets Canadians with fake AI news for profit, CBC/Radio-Canada investigation reveals
candidates.description: An investigation by CBC's visual investigations team and Radio-Canada's Décrypteurs has discovered a Vietnamese company is linked to a network of Facebook pages and websites sharing misleading, sensationalist or outright false news headlines.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The U.S. is considering a federal tax incentive for films. How might that affect Canada?
candidates.description: Amid the buzz surrounding the upcoming Toronto International Film Festival, U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed the creation of a federal tax incentive to keep film production in the U.S. instead of seeing it move to other countries – calling out Canada by name. But is it fair to frame the Hollywood exodus as Canada taking jobs from the U.S.?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. military says it destroyed 5 more Iranian oil tankers in latest escalation
candidates.description: The U.S. military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to recent attacks on its warships, and Tehran says it hit back at American targets in Jordan, in the latest burst of back-and-forth strikes in a more than six-month-old war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada, U.K., France to ban trade of goods from Israeli settlements in occupied West Bank
candidates.description: Canada, Britain and France say they will ban the trade of goods with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The U.K. is going a step further by implementing fresh sanctions and saying it will take additional action against companies and individuals that support settlement expansion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: NTSB investigators to interview pilots of crashed Amazon cargo jet Wednesday
candidates.description: The U.S. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) says it will interview the two pilots who survived the crash Sunday of their Amazon cargo jet in Miami. The NTSB says its has already obtained data from the voice recorder that was recovered from the aircraft Monday, but will not release it yet.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband threatens legal action over 'relentless' conspiracy theories
candidates.description: Patrick Clancy was ruled out as a suspect in the 2023 deaths of his children, Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and eight-month-old Callan. His ex-wife Lindsay Clancy's murder trial, which ended last Friday in a mistrial, has captivated spectators from the beginning. But misinformation and conspiracy theories involving Patrick have swirled online, prompting threats of lawsuits.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iceland summons U.S. ambassador over Trump's threat to take over Arctic nation
candidates.description: Over the holiday long weekend, U.S. President Donald Trump posted to his social media a map featuring the red, white and blue stars and stripes of the U.S. flag draped across all of North America — including Mexico, Canada, Greenland and Iceland. The move prompted Iceland to summon its ambassador.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's new tariffs: Are small businesses 'cannon fodder' in the trade war?
candidates.description: Experts say Canada's new tariffs will have an outsized impact on the country's small and medium-sized businesses, with few consequences for individual consumers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump to Canadian plane maker Bombardier: You can't sell in U.S. unless you build in U.S.
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump says Bombardier would no longer be allowed to sell in the U.S. unless ​the Montreal-based airplane company starts manufacturing in the states.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Grindr to pay $48-million settlement over sale of users' info — including HIV status
candidates.description: The hookup app Grindr is on the hook for a huge payout after settling a U.K. lawsuit that alleged sensitive information about its users — including their HIV status — was sold to advertisers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Germany's Merz attacks AfD in stormy debate after far-right election win
candidates.description: Germany's chancellor clashes with AfD leader Alice Weidel, saying her migration policy amounts to "ethnic cleansing" for skilled workers.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Oil hits $100 a barrel for first time since July after US and Houthi strikes
candidates.description: Brent crude - the global benchmark for prices - rises after the US hit five Iranian tankers on Tuesday
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US to ban imports of some Canadian alcohol, dairy goods and motorbikes
candidates.description: It is the latest strike in a long trade war, and comes after Canadian counter-tariffs on US goods come into force.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Uganda pulling out of Prince Harry's Invictus Games, says military chief
candidates.description: The decision, announced by the chief of defence, comes just two months after Uganda said it would participate.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Baby orangutans found in Indian forest spark trafficking inquiry
candidates.description: The critically endangered apes were found far from their natural habitat in the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hong Kong's first leader after British handover dies
candidates.description: The tenure of Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader after Britain handed over the city to China, was marked by crises and protests.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Meta continues to run ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India - report
candidates.description: The report follows a BBC Eye investigation that found Instagram running paid ads promoting such material in India.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Constantly on my mind' - 9/11 agony endures for bereaved, 25 years on
candidates.description: As the 25th anniversary approaches, the wait for the alleged mastermind of the attack to be put on trial goes on.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: British-Israeli relations at lowest ebb in decades
candidates.description: Israel's response to London's trade ban with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank shows how important this moment is.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hegseth is shaking up the Pentagon as the US wages war - but at what cost?
candidates.description: The upheaval in the military could shape the legacy of Trump's second term, writes the BBC's Tom Bateman.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Norway bids farewell to King Harald
candidates.description: Tens of thousands of people lined the streets to pay their respects after 13 days of national mourning.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Where is Israel's proposed West Bank settlement the UK opposes?
candidates.description: BBC's Middle East correspondent Lucy Williamson reports from an area close to Israel's proposed site in the occupied West Bank.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pupils return to West Bank school behind barbed wire to protect against settlers
candidates.description: Six people, including three pupils at the Palestinian school, have been killed in al-Mughayyir this year, in a surge of Israeli settler-related violence.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Good to have choice': Australians on opting out of social media algorithms
candidates.description: The BBC spoke to people in Sydney about Australia's plans to force social media companies to allow users to easily opt in or out of personalised algorithms.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Apple unveils its first folding iPhone
candidates.description: Apple showed off at an event the first major design change to the iPhone in almost 20 years.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'
candidates.description: It is the latest in a series of increasing warnings about the safety threat posed by artificial intelligence.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: New law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images
candidates.description: The government said it will legislate "as soon as they can" but may "reassess" its plans if firms make the desired changes sooner.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Scammers demand ransoms from Instagram users over fake copyright claims
candidates.description: Users say they are losing money or risk having their accounts suspended because Meta struggles to identify scammers.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Downed trees and flooding as Hurricane Lowell batters western Hawaii
candidates.description: The storm brought damaging winds and torrential rain to parts of the island on Monday and Tuesday, triggering concerns about flash flooding and mudslides.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem
candidates.description: A curious online row over this summer's heatwaves points to a wider - and worrying - shift in climate science.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Backshall backs calls for natural history GCSE
candidates.description: Steve Backshall calls for nature education as a survey says 55% of children have not climbed a tree.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Greetings from Paris, where the 2024 Olympics balloon rises again
candidates.description: The floating Olympic cauldron, held aloft by a giant glowing balloon, is still making regular appearances two years after the 2024 Paris Games, showing up all summer long in the nighttime Paris sky.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. military destroys 5 Iranian oil tankers. And, the Smithsonian head resigns
candidates.description: The U.S. military says it has destroyed five Iranian oil tankers as the conflict continues to escalate. And, Smithsonian head Lonnie G. Bunch III says he plans to step down by the end of the year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
candidates.description: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Iceland summons U.S. ambassador after Trump posts countries draped with American flag
candidates.description: Iceland summoned the U.S. ambassador after President Trump posted a map on Truth Social that showed the country, along with a number of other nations, covered with an American flag.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. military says it destroyed 5 Iranian oil tankers after attacks on Navy warship
candidates.description: The U.S. military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to the latest attacks on its warships. Iran hit American targets in Jordan.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Australian social media users to be offered choice to opt out of algorithms
candidates.description: A government statement said on Tuesday social media platforms would be required to send a notification to new and existing users offering them a choice over their default feed.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.K. accuses Israeli settlers of 'ethnic cleansing' in West Bank and bans their goods
candidates.description: France, Canada and other countries joined the U.K. in banning goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Israel said it would close the British Consulate among other measures.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: GOP to host unusual midterm convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect
candidates.description: Republicans are aiming to get voters to turn out for the midterms with an unconventional convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on the U.S. went into effect at midnight.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Chrystia Freeland negotiated with Trump. Now she's watching a trade war unfold
candidates.description: Chrystia Freeland understands the U.S.-Canada relationship from her time at the negotiating table. Here's what she sees now.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fold the phone: Apple's new CEO unveils a foldable iPhone
candidates.description: New Apple CEO John Ternus announces the iPhone Duo, which folds like a passport and is the most radical iPhone design update in nearly 20 years.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new Anthropic model seeks to test how AI could impact the U.S. economy
candidates.description: Will artificial intelligence nibble around the edges of the economy or upend it altogether? A new, interactive model from Anthropic lets people tests their assumptions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Has the economy gone C-shaped?
candidates.description: A K means the rich and poor are pulling apart. A C supposedly means they're coming back together. We hear the case for both. Which letter you see may depend on what you choose to pay attention to.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What to know about Canada's escalating trade war with the U.S.
candidates.description: Canada struck back at U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday with tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods. The outcome could resonate far beyond Canada.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Union electricians welcome data center boom
candidates.description: The boom in data centers has brought plenty of work and lots of overtime to union electricians, putting them at odds with many communities trying to block new data center construction.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
candidates.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Whatever happened to the measles outbreak that shocked a country this year?
candidates.description: Bangladesh has seen over 50,000 confirmed or suspected cases of measles this year. The death toll among children just surpassed 1,000. How are officials trying to bring the outbreak under control?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How to fight with the people we care about, illustrated
candidates.description: Arguing with a partner or a loved one can be anxiety-inducing. Conflict resolution facilitator Priya Parker explains how to start and end a fight — while easing dread for everyone.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A Louisiana case could upend telehealth abortion. What exactly is it?
candidates.description: As a federal appeals court considers Louisiana's lawsuit to end telehealth abortion access, a longtime OB-GYN in Arizona explains how telehealth works in his clinic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Whatever happened to the Taliban threat: 'We will flog the women'?
candidates.description: In 2024, the ruling Taliban pledged to use flogging as well as stoning to punish people for not following certain of their precepts — committing adultery, running secret schools for girls. Have they followed through?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The copper peptide trend has gone from creams to injections — ahead of the science
candidates.description: Copper peptides are among the biggest viral trends on social media. Does evidence support smearing on the electric blue tincture for firmer skin, wound healing and other anti-aging effects?
candidates.author: NPR

Unlike conventional methods that model navigation as a 2D path planning problem, humanoid traversal in cluttered environments requires continuous geometry-aware whole-body adaptation, including coordinated arm placement, torso adjustment, and gait modulation for collision-free movement through complex 3D spaces. We introduce TANGO, the first whole-body vision-language navigation framework for language-conditioned humanoid traversal in cluttered environments. Given a natural-language instruction and egocentric RGB observations, TANGO directly predicts 29-DoF joint-space actions for downstream whole-body control. We train TANGO entirely in simulation by synthesizing diverse collision-free traversal behaviors via global path planning, kinematic whole-body motion generation, obstacle-aware motion editing, and RL-based tracking. This pipeline provides dynamically feasible action supervision for learning language-conditioned whole-body policies. In extensive simulation experiments, TANGO demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in vision-language navigation, while outperforming strong modular baselines in navigating challenging scenes requiring obstacle negotiation. Lastly, we deploy TANGO zero-shot on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, and observe robust language-guided traversal in cluttered real-world scenes without training on any real-world navigation data.
candidates.author: Anqi Li, Yuxin Chen, Zhaobo Li, Zhuo Cao, Junli Ren, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Dhruv Shah

candidates.title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models
candidates.description: Recurrent models provide a natural path to long-context modeling, yet models trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT) often fail beyond their training horizon. Classical analyses emphasize gradients that vanish or explode along temporal paths. However, dense per-token losses can still train a shared recurrent rule despite severe decay, showing that decay alone does not determine whether learning fails. We instead study state credit: the signal through which future losses reach earlier recurrent states before contributing to parameter updates. Accordingly, we intervene directly on state credit and propose Credit Stabilization through Time (CST). During backward propagation, CST locally rescales the state-credit signal to stabilize its norm without rotating the component being corrected, while leaving the forward computation unchanged. Because controlled synthetic tasks and real data exhibit different credit dynamics, we specialize CST to each regime. In both settings, CST improves performance beyond the training horizon, with gains observed at up to 128x the training length.
candidates.author: Hanwen Jiang

candidates.title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation
candidates.description: Accurate citations are the foundation of academic writing, tracing intellectual origins and substantiating core claims. However, manually navigating the growing volume of scientific literature is increasingly difficult, prompting reliance on automatic citation recommendation. While modern retrieval-augmented architectures have largely mitigated the fabrication of non-existent papers, current systems relying on semantic similarity struggle with misattribution, often citing authentic papers that fail to logically support the author's claim. To address this challenge, we argue that accurate citation requires a shift from similarity-based search to active, claim-level reasoning. We propose ReCite, a decoupled agentic framework that orchestrates location perception, intent-aware query planning, and reflective verification. Trained on synthesized reasoning trajectories, our agent verifies claim-evidence consistency and triggers self-correction loops when retrieved candidates lack logical support. Experiments demonstrate that our lightweight framework outperforms state-of-the-art massive generative models in strict citation accuracy. By grounding literature matching in verifiable logic rather than semantic overlap, ReCite establishes a reliable foundation for automated academic writing.
candidates.author: Yuyang Huang, Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Yuzhe Ding, Chong Teng, Fei Li, Donghong Ji

candidates.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
candidates.description: Large language models are increasingly deployed as agents that plan over long horizons and act through external tools. Most agents select actions through unconstrained generation over an accumulating history, leaving implicit the procedural knowledge of what to do, in what order, and under which conditions. As trajectories lengthen, agents can lose track of their objectives, invoke tools out of order, and repeat unproductive actions. We introduce the Procedural Graph: just as a knowledge graph organizes factual knowledge into (entity, relation, entity) triplets for what-is questions, a Procedural Graph organizes procedural knowledge into (procedure, relation, procedure) triplets for what-to-do questions. At each decision step, the framework localizes the agent's active node, and a guidance model translates the surrounding subgraph into step-level situational guidance that biases the solver's next action without dictating it. The graph is self-evolving: an LLM refiner contrasts failed trajectories with successful ones and edits the graph's topology and attributes, committing edits that preserve or improve held-out validation performance while retaining rejected ones to discourage repetition. Starting from a minimal skeleton, the loop builds graphs that match or surpass hand-designed ones. It can also repair a flawed expert prior. Across multiple datasets, task types, and LLMs, the Procedural Graph delivers consistent gains over memory-based baselines, and self-evolution further improves performance without manual engineering.
candidates.author: Yuxing Lu, Yicheng Chen, Shanchan Wu, Sercan Ö. Arık

candidates.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
candidates.description: In June 2026, thousands of AI agents found that a small public wiki would accept edits from inside their sandboxes, and started using it to help one another pass a timed test. Each agent lived for about an hour and remembered nothing afterwards. Nobody asked them to cooperate, and the wiki had not been built for them. The complete record of what they wrote is public, and it is unusually informative, because it preserves not only what each agent wrote but what that agent could see before writing. We use it to follow the three decisions an agent had to make on arrival: where to write, what to call itself, and how to word its message. One rule governs all three. An agent takes an option with a probability close to the share of that option in what it can see, and the share that matters is the one on the page in front of it, then the one in the stream of recent edits, and only weakly anything older. Three minimal copying models, one per decision and with a single free parameter each, reproduce the heavy-tailed distribution of how many agents met on a page, the frequency of the pieces from which the agents built their names, and the patchwork of pages that are internally consistent and different from one another. Copying whatever the environment happens to show is enough to produce most of the collective structure of this population. It is also what makes such a population easy to steer, since whoever writes first, or writes while the others are quiet, sets the convention for everyone who comes later.
candidates.author: Giordano De Marzo, Nicola Albore, David Garcia

candidates.title: Proxy Policy Steering
candidates.description: Generalist robot policies carry broad manipulation priors from large-scale data, but specializing them to a new task remains the deployment bottleneck. This requires eliciting task-specific behavior from limited demonstrations without degrading their broad capabilities. We introduce Proxy Policy Steering (PPS), an inference-time adaptation method that resolves this challenge by training two lightweight proxy policies whose calibrated velocity-space difference steers the frozen base sampler. A reference proxy models the frozen base's behavior on target-task observations, and a task proxy, initialized from the reference, captures how this behavior changes under task supervision. Their difference forms a calibrated velocity-space residual that steers the frozen base sampler at every denoising step. We identify the conditions under which this residual isolates the change induced by task supervision, and validate them empirically. Because the base is never directly modified, its broad capabilities remain available at inference, including behaviors such as recovery from failure that the demonstrations themselves do not exercise. Adaptation requires only forward velocity predictions from the base, making PPS lightweight to train and applicable even without access to the base's parameters. On 8 real-world and 4 simulation manipulation tasks, PPS lifts the state-of-the-art pi 0.5 base policy by 53% absolute success rate on average, with zero-to-one gains on tasks the base never solves, while preserving the base's broad capabilities. PPS outperforms LoRA fine-tuning, from-scratch specialists, residual policies, and prior inference-time steering methods.
candidates.author: Chuanruo Ning, Tianrui Wang, Wei-Chiu Ma, Kuan Fang

candidates.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models
candidates.description: Image tokenizers define the ``visual language'' of unified multimodal models, yet are commonly studied through isolated metrics or generation-/understanding-only evaluations. These evaluations do not fully capture how visual tokens behave when modeled jointly with text. We build a controlled pure-autoregressive testbed and track task-specific validation losses during multimodal continual pretraining across text, image, text-to-image (T2I), and image-to-text (I2T) prediction. We examine how these losses scale and relate to downstream performance, then use them to study multimodal learnability---how well image and text tokens are jointly modeled---and tokenizer design. We find that (1) losses should be analyzed by task, since they exhibit distinct scaling behavior and rank tokenizers differently. (2) The loss--performance relationship depends on the predicted token space: for a fixed tokenizer, T2I and I2T losses correlate with generation quality, but across tokenizers, the T2I loss--performance relationship shifts with the image-token space, whereas I2T loss, computed over a shared text vocabulary, provides a more consistent signal. I2T loss also correlates with both generation and visual understanding performance after supervised finetuning. Using losses as a lens, we show that (3) better reconstruction does not necessarily yield lower task-specific losses or stronger downstream performance, and that (4) image tokenizer choice can affect text modeling under joint optimization. As case studies, we revisit three tokenizer design axes---the discriminator, semantic supervision, and vocabulary size---to examine their effects on joint modeling and downstream performance. Together, our testbed offers a complementary perspective on image tokenizers as visual languages, highlighting their interplay with text in joint multimodal training.
candidates.author: Siting Li, Zhengyang Wang, Simon Shaolei Du, Xi Chen, Yang Liu

candidates.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting
candidates.description: The digitization of healthcare has generated vast, longitudinal, and multimodal patient records over a lifetime, yet fully exploiting these data to represent and predict patient state trajectories remains a critical challenge. Current AI models often struggle to capture the complex, irregular temporal dynamics and inherent stochasticity of real-world multimodal patient data. Existing AI approaches for modeling longitudinal patient records are predominantly discriminative, limited to a few modalities, constrained by closed categorical vocabularies, treating time as a monotonic inductive bias, or they are limited in forecasting future patient states. We introduce NOAH, a time-aware, task-agnostic, generative transformer model representing and forecasting the full multimodal patient journey. NOAH features a novel bidirectional time integration and a variational latent space to capture the continuous evolution of patient states and the stochasticity of clinical trajectories. Built from over 559 million clinical events from 431,000 hospital visits of 299,000 patients across the MIMIC dataset family, NOAH natively processes medical images, time-series and numeric signals, categorical events, as well as structured and unstructured clinical records. NOAH is the first truly holistic generative model in its field, enabling autoregressive forecasting with optional time control, zero-shot classification, and counterfactual intervention simulation. It generates highly informative and predictive patient state representations that demonstrate strong performance in probing for clinical outcomes, 15 ICD chapters, and 29 comorbidities, as well as in time-to-event prediction. Seamlessly handling diverse modalities and complex temporal dynamics, NOAH provides a versatile, task-agnostic, scalable foundation for intelligent predictive systems in personalized clinical care and digital medicine.
candidates.author: Tobias Susetzky, Raphael Rehms, Dmitrii Seletkov, Özgün Turgut, Michelle Espranita Liman, Lisa Steinhelfer, Rickmer Braren, Daniel Rueckert

candidates.title: A Data-Driven Framework for Identifying and Prioritizing RPA Opportunities in Healthcare Processes
candidates.description: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is widely used to reduce administrative burden in United States hospitals, yet an estimated 30-50% of RPA initiatives underperform because processes are selected informally, without a repeatable method to catalogue candidates, prioritize them, match each to an automation tier -- a Python bot, an open-source orchestrator such as n8n, or an enterprise platform such as UiPath -- and forecast financial return before committing resources. We propose a four-module, data-driven framework unifying these decisions: a Process Taxonomy of twenty recurring hospital processes across five value streams; a Prioritization module deriving an Automation Suitability Index from an Analytic Hierarchy Process matrix with an explicit consistency check; a Tool-Tier Selection module recommending the least-cost technology sufficient for a process complexity, integration, and compliance profile; and a Return-on-Investment module quantifying labor savings, error-cost avoidance, payback, and net present value. Applied to a synthetic portfolio spanning all twenty processes, plus a reference data-flow architecture linking it to hospital EHR/payer/ERP systems: 12 of 20 clear the prioritization threshold; the ranking is robust to +/-20% weight perturbation (Spearman correlation 0.83, top-5 set preserved 97.7%, 2,000 Monte Carlo trials); an Automation Risk Index flags four qualifying processes as Critical risk; a budget-constrained portfolio optimization shows diminishing marginal NPV as spend scales from $400K to $1.03M; and a second Monte Carlo analysis shows portfolio NPV stays positive at its 5th percentile. The framework is a conceptual synthesis of the literature rather than an instrument calibrated on primary hospital data; we discuss HIPAA governance and a research agenda for empirical validation. A supplementary Python implementation accompanies the paper.
candidates.author: Maria Alejandra Gomez, Juan Manuel Castillo

candidates.title: Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation
candidates.description: Existing methods for test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) derive rewards from answer-level self-voting on unlabeled test-time tasks with canonical answers, but this breaks down for code generation because programs cannot be compared by surface form and therefore do not directly provide a usable training signal. To make TTRL applicable to code generation, we propose probe-driven TTRL, which constructs output-free probe inputs from the problem statement, executes candidate programs on these probes, and defines a Probe Consensus Reward (PCR) from the resulting behavioral agreement. PCR provides a behavioral training signal for open-vocabulary programs, but it is not a fully reliable verifier and remains susceptible to reward hacking through spurious consensus. We therefore introduce Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization (ERPO), which converts low PCR into conservative negative updates through rank masking and controls policy drift with an entropy ceiling. On coding benchmarks, ERPO substantially improves pass@1 and pass@k in both in-domain adaptation and zero-shot transfer.
candidates.author: Jiacheng Xu, Feng Chen, Xiuneng Xu, Bo An

candidates.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
candidates.description: Agent harnesses (the system prompt, tool set, execution hooks, and context-management scaffolding around a model) are a critical determinant of agentic task success. Automated harness evolution can enable smaller models to perform well on domain-specific tasks at a fraction of frontier-model cost. Since both the harness and model weights shape behavior, we ask how harness evolution and lightweight fine-tuning should be combined. Across seven enterprise agent tasks, we first evolve a harness with the weaker model, then find that a stronger expert often uses it more effectively, suggesting expert supervision could close the remaining gap. However, training the weaker model on the expert's complete trajectories under the evolved harness backfires: performance regresses on all seven tasks by 4 to 30 points across Qwen3-Coder and Gemma 4, even though the same procedure helps under the unevolved harness. Our analysis shows that imitation transfers knowledge and increases scaffold usage, but disrupts model-harness fit: the weaker model adopts the expert's planning strategy without the competence to execute it and no longer matches the harness evolved around its native planning style. We therefore develop an on-policy expert-correction pipeline, automated by a meta-level MLE agent, that localizes the failing turn in the weaker model's own rollout and asks the expert to rewrite only that turn. This preserves the model's planning style and combines the gains of harness evolution and model adaptation. Our results identify and resolve a source of contention between harness and weight updates, yielding a compatibility-preserving recipe for economical co-evolution on domain-specific enterprise tasks.
candidates.author: Zhou Yu, Bin Bi, Shiva Kumar Pentyala, Shubham Mehrotra, Sougata Chaudhuri, Shilpa Bhagavath, Zeyuan Chen, Ran Xu, Phil Mui, James Zhu, Sitaram Asur

candidates.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents
candidates.description: Execution feedback can guide coding agents toward correct repository repairs, but only when the tests capture the behavior requested by the issue. Agent-generated tests can encode incomplete or incorrect behavioral targets; when the same trajectory writes both the patch and the test, their errors can agree and create false confidence. We introduce ExecCritic, combining a test--verify--revise scaffold with a role-specific reinforcement learning recipe for training agents within it. The scaffold separates test construction from source-code repair: a Test agent independently generates repository-native tests, a fail-closed harness qualifies and freezes them, and a Repair agent revises source code from their execution feedback without changing the tests. Both roles use Qwen-3.5-35B-A3B as the backbone and are trained separately. In Learn to Test, the Test agent learns to produce behaviorally valid tests that distinguish correct from incorrect patches. In Test to Improve, the Repair agent learns both direct task resolution and feedback-guided revision. On SWE-bench Verified, test quality determines whether feedback helps: holding the base Repair agent fixed, tests from the base Test agent reduce resolved rate from a no-test baseline of 61.2% to 57.3%, whereas tests from GPT-5.6-sol raise it to 65.3%. Role-specific post-training raises the Qwen Test agent's Base-to-Gold success from 22.2% to 62.2%; composing the two post-trained Qwen agents reaches 72.6%, an 11.4-point gain over the original no-test baseline without stronger-model or Oracle feedback at evaluation time. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/execcritic.
candidates.author: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Haorui Wang, Hang Wang, Hao Cheng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Tao Ge, Sharon Li, Jianfeng Gao
